name: Apples
plantSpacingText: Dwarf systems may space ~4–10 ft; semi-dwarf/standard trees need much more

name: Arborvitae / Northern White-Cedar
plantSpacingText: cultivar-specific: dwarf forms to 10–15 ft-wide species plants

name: Arugula
plantSpacingText: 2-4 in for baby leaf; 6 in for mature plants

name: Asparagus
plantSpacingText: crowns commonly about 12 in apart; rows much wider

name: Beans
plantSpacingText: Bush beans 4-6 in; pole beans 6-8 in with support

name: Beets
plantSpacingText: 3-4 in between plants; 12-18 in between rows

name: Blackberries
plantSpacingText: 36–60 in between plants; rows usually much wider

name: Blueberries
plantSpacingText: about 3 ft for compact northern types; larger cultivars require more

name: Bok Choy
plantSpacingText: 6-12 in depending on full-size or baby harvest

name: Bonnie Little Bing Compact Cherry Tomato
Bonnie Little Sicily Slicing Tomato SFG
Boxwood
plantSpacingText: spacing depends strongly on cultivar and hedge intent

name: Broccoli Rabe / Rapini
plantSpacingText: 4–8 in for individual plants; denser sowing for baby greens

name: Brussels Sprouts
plantSpacingText: about 18 in between plants; wider spacing can improve airflow

name: Cantaloupe / Muskmelon
plantSpacingText: 3–5 ft between plants for field-grown vines

name: Carrots
plantSpacingText: 1-3 in after thinning; 12-18 in between rows

name: Celery
plantSpacingText: about 6–12 in depending on cultivar and desired stalk size

name: Cilantro
plantSpacingText: 4–8 in for leaf harvest; can be denser for baby foliage

name: Collards
plantSpacingText: 12-18 in for regular harvest; wider for full plants

name: Corn
plantSpacingText: 8-12 in in blocks; 24-36 in between rows

name: Cucumbers
plantSpacingText: 12-18 in on trellis; more for sprawling plants

name: Daffodil
plantSpacingText: typically 4–6 in apart for naturalized groups

name: Fennel
plantSpacingText: 12–18 in for bulb fennel; herb fennel may be wider

name: Fig
plantSpacingText: allow roughly 8–15 ft for in-ground plants; containers can be much smaller

name: Garlic
plantSpacingText: 4-6 in between cloves; 8-12 in between rows

name: Geranium / Pelargonium
plantSpacingText: 8–12 in for common zonal types; larger cultivars need more

name: Grapes
plantSpacingText: commonly 6–8 ft between backyard vines; system and vigor vary

name: Hosta
plantSpacingText: cultivar range is enormous; 12–36 in is a useful common planning span

name: Japanese Maple
plantSpacingText: 10–25 ft spread for the species; dwarf cultivars can be far smaller

name: Leeks
plantSpacingText: 4–6 in between plants for mature shanks

name: Marigold
plantSpacingText: 6–18 in depending on French/African cultivar size

name: Mizuna
plantSpacingText: 4-8 in for cut greens; wider for full plants

name: Onions
plantSpacingText: 4-6 in for bulbs; closer for scallions

name: Parsley
plantSpacingText: 6–12 in depending on leaf type and harvest style

name: Peaches
plantSpacingText: traditional planting often about 14 × 22 ft; dwarfing/training changes this greatly

name: Peas
plantSpacingText: 2-3 in with support for taller varieties

name: Peppers
plantSpacingText: 18-24 in between plants; 24-36 in between rows

name: Petunia
plantSpacingText: 1–3 ft depending on hybrid group and trailing habit

name: Potatoes
plantSpacingText: 10-12 in between seed pieces; 30-36 in between rows

name: Pumpkin
plantSpacingText: vining pumpkins commonly 2–5 ft between plants; compact types can be closer

name: Radishes
plantSpacingText: 1-2 in for small radishes; more for daikon

name: Raspberries
plantSpacingText: often 2–3 ft between red raspberry plants; systems vary

name: Rhubarb
plantSpacingText: allow roughly a 3 × 3 ft area per plant

name: Rose — Garden / Hybrid
plantSpacingText: 2–6 ft common shrub-rose spacing; climbers and miniatures differ

name: Rosemary
plantSpacingText: 18–36 in depending on cultivar and pruning

name: Scallions / Green Onions
plantSpacingText: about 1 in apart for bunching scallions

name: Sour Cherries
plantSpacingText: traditional red tart cherry spacing about 20 × 25 ft; dwarf rootstocks can be closer

name: Spinach
plantSpacingText: 4-6 in for mature plants; closer for baby leaf

name: Strawberries
plantSpacingText: 12–18 in basic spacing; 18–24 in common matted-row systems

name: Sunflower
plantSpacingText: 12–24 in for many garden cultivars; dwarf and giant types differ

name: Sweet Cherries
plantSpacingText: spacing is strongly rootstock-dependent; standard orchards can use ~25 × 30 ft

name: Tomatillo
plantSpacingText: allow up to about 3 ft because plants become bushy

name: Tomatoes
plantSpacingText: 18-24 in between plants; 30-36 in between rows

name: Tulip
plantSpacingText: commonly 4–6 in apart in display plantings

name: Turnips
plantSpacingText: 2-4 in for small roots; wider for large varieties

name: Watermelon
plantSpacingText: 3–6 ft between plants for field-grown vines
